projects.name: MaineDOT Construction Advertise Plan - Line
projects.notes: MaineDOT's Construction Advertise Plan: projects the department plans to advertise for bids in the plan year (PLAN_YEAR = '2026' for every record on the check date; the layer is refreshed daily and should roll to the next year when MaineDOT publishes the new plan). So these are funded projects about to be let, not long-range plans. ADV_DATE is the planned advertise date as TEXT 'MM/DD/YYYY'. MRE is the most recent estimate as a number (MOST_RECENT_EST is the same as text, e.g. '$765,000'). SCOPE_DESC is the scope of work; WORKTYPE is the broader programme (Bridge Construction, Bridges Other, Highway Construction, Highway Light Capital Paving, Highway Preservation Paving, Highway Rehabilitation, Highway Safety and Spot Improvements, Maintenance, Multimodal). No status field and no county field: TOWNS lists the town(s). The sibling 'Construction Advertise Schedule' services (same names with Schedule instead of Plan) add CURR_FORECAST_DATE, ACTUAL_ADV_DATE and CHANGE_STATUS (e.g. 'On Time') to show which have already been advertised.

projects.name: MaineDOT Construction Advertise Plan - Point
projects.notes: Point projects (bridges, culverts, signals, intersections) of the same advertise plan; fields assumed identical to the line layer (only the count and the SCOPE_DESC values were pulled for this layer - confirm with one sample record). A third service, Construction_Advertise_Plan_-_Polygon (254 records), is lines and points combined as buffered polygons.

projects.name: MaineDOT All Capital Projects
projects.notes: Every MaineDOT capital project, past and future, as buffered POLYGONS (not lines). Filter WORK_STATUS IN ('Planned','Candidate') for future work (6,636 records are 'Planned'); 'Underway' is under construction, 'Accomplished' is done. No cost, date or town fields - join to the advertise plan by PIN where possible. PRIMARY_WORK_DESC has 103 distinct values (many legacy ones ending '(OLD)'); only a selection is listed. STATUS is an internal code (01-92, CANDREQ, ROWONLY) - 'ROWONLY' looks like right-of-way-only projects but that meaning was not confirmed. RTCODE/BMP/EMP are route and begin/end mile points.

parcels_statewide.name: Maine Parcels Organized Towns (Maine GeoLibrary) - polygons + ADB assessment table
parcels_statewide.notes: PARTIAL statewide. Towns submit data voluntarily: the polygon layer holds parcels for about 319 town codes (GEOCODE) across all 16 counties, but the owner table (layer 9, Maine_Parcels_Organized_Towns_ADB) only has rows for 211 town codes, and 459,454 rows have a non-blank OWNER1. The polygon layer itself has NO owner; join the table on STATE_ID (town GEOCODE + '_' + MAP_BK_LOT, e.g. '09030_101-001-000'). Data age varies by town (FMUPDAT on polygons, e.g. 2010; YEAR_CREAT on the table, e.g. 2023; YEAR_CREAT has many junk values) so owners can be years out of date. OWNER2 is a second owner; LS_DATE / LS_PRICE are the last sale; LOT_SIZE was null in the sample. Blanks are often a single space. No restriction stated on the service. The unorganized territory is a separate layer (https://services1.arcgis.com/RbMX0mRVOFNTdLzd/arcgis/rest/services/Maine_Unorganized_Parcel_Layers_view/FeatureServer/0, 36,282 parcels, answered) with no owner-name field.

summary: Projects work: MaineDOT's advertise plan gives this year's lettings as lines and points with scope, estimate and advertise date, and an all-projects polygon layer has a Planned/Candidate status. Parcels are partial: a state layer has owner and mailing address for roughly 211 of the organized towns via a joined table; other towns have boundaries only and data age varies. County-level sources were not researched because Maine parcels are kept by towns, not counties.
